title: Poland moves SAFE from legislative authorization to a reported domestic defense-contracting wave
source_unit: Polish Sejm SAFE legislative process and Polish Ministry of National Defence implementation summaries
geography: Poland; Polish defense industry and armed forces

observations.period: February 2026; Sejm government SAFE bill, druk 2227

denominator.unit: government bill and parliamentary legislative process

safe_legislative_framework.value: SAFE financing instrument enacted through the parliamentary process for defense-investment financing

financing_route.value: dedicated SAFE financing routed through a Polish institutional framework and defense-fund mechanism

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official Sejm legislative-process page for the government SAFE bill. The parliamentary authorization stage is kept separate from later contracts, obligations, delivery, and capability realization.
observations.uncertainty: The process page does not by itself establish the amount drawn, contract performance, supplier shares, delivery, acceptance, or operational effect. Procedural metadata is not a public-opinion or household-incidence measure.
observations.subgroup: Polish national legislative and defense-financing institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Legislative authorization can create a financing route without proving that funds are drawn, that domestic firms receive the intended work, or that capability and independence improve.

denominator.unit: SAFE-financed contracts reported by the Polish Armament Agency and Cyber Defense Component

reported_recipient_scope.value: all contracts stated by MON to have been concluded with Polish defense industry

reported_borsuk_quantity.unit: Borsuk infantry fighting vehicles in listed contract scope

reported_flyeye_quantity.unit: FlyEye unmanned-system sets in listed contract scope

reported_warmate_quantity.unit: minimum; Warmate sets in listed contract scope

reported_san_modules.unit: SAN air-defense fire modules in listed contract scope

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official Polish Ministry of National Defence SAFE program page. Contract count, reported value, recipient category, and selected listed equipment scopes are retained as signed-contract observations, not pooled delivered quantities.
observations.uncertainty: The page does not provide full contract texts, obligations, payment schedules, supplier-level value shares, delivery dates, acceptance records, or evidence that any listed item was delivered. The source-level category ‘Polish defense industry’ does not establish domestic control of critical components, design authority, or replaceability.
observations.subgroup: Polish Armament Agency and Cyber Defense Component SAFE contracts with the Polish defense industry.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large signed-contract wave can strengthen expected domestic demand and industrial workload while leaving execution, imported inputs, workforce effects, delivery, and operational readiness unresolved.

observations.period: 2026-06-01; MON public implementation and strategic framing summary

denominator.unit: official Ministry of National Defence implementation summary and senior-official statements

domestic_security_framing.value: SAFE is framed as Polish equipment for the Polish armed forces and as an investment in future generations' security

production_independence_framing.value: the summary links the program to greater operational capability and day-to-day independence of defense production

industrial_contracting_summary.unit: contracts reported as signed in three days

observations.method: Translation-neutral extraction of the official MON implementation summary and statements. Contracting facts and institutional meaning claims are retained separately from independently measured output, public reception, or sovereignty.
observations.uncertainty: The summary is an official account and does not independently verify contract performance, delivery, acceptance, local-content shares, public approval, or strategic leverage. Rhetorical claims about expectations and independence are not outcome measures.
observations.subgroup: Polish defense, government, and armed-forces institutions communicating SAFE implementation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Institutional claims about patriotism, public expectations, and independence can legitimate borrowing and procurement while coexist­ing with foreign technology, components, finance, and approval dependence.

related_sources.claim: Normalized local note preserves the legislative, contract-count, value, scope, and interpretation boundaries.
CBOS supplies the separate public-judgment layer about competing defense-financing routes.
The Poland-US record supplies the separate reciprocal-access, Barracuda co-production, and implementation-stage route.
MON supplies the official count, amount, listed equipment scopes, and Polish-defense-industry recipient category for SAFE contracts.

boundary: This record establishes a Polish legislative and institutional contracting action under SAFE, plus official domestic-industry and independence framing. It does not establish Barracuda inclusion, contract performance, plant commissioning, completed output, acceptance, delivery, local-content shares, household incidence, public reception, or geopolitical leverage. Signed contracts are not delivered capability.
